newsitem.title: USA: IMF sees favorable 1997 outlook for China.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees favorable 1997 outlook for China.

text.p: China's economic outlook remains favorable this year after achieving a soft landing in 1996 from three years of double-digit inflation, the International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday.
The IMF said it expected China's economy to grow by 9.5 percent in 1997, down slightly from 9.7 percent seen for 1996. Inflation would remain steady at six percent.
"Like many other rapidly growing economies in Asia, China has taken measures to reduce overheating," the IMF's World Economic Outlook said, adding that the stage was set for continued expansion.

But sustaining rapid growth with low inflation would require progress in restructuring and raising efficiency in state enterprises, including by diversifying ownership. And progress was also needed in addressing weaknesses in the financial sector and in enhancing budget revenue, it said.

The strong external sector provided the opportunity to accelerate significantly the process of trade liberalization, the report said, saying freer trade was critical for China to benefit fully from the recent implementation of current account convertibility.
